The change adds a per-ledger async mutex so that paid work sharing a scoped budget is admitted serially, acquiring admission in `complete_ladder` and after the non-agentic fallback in `review`, and set on `scoped_budget`. The three new tests exercise the reachable paths (concurrent affordable completions admitted after settlement, unbounded fan-out still refused before dispatch, a fresh scope not blocked by its parent's queue, and a cancelled waiter releasing admission without dispatching), and each asserts on observable behaviour — provider request count, per-call usage, and the error on the denied call — rather than on the mutex. I found no defect worth blocking on.

The change adds a `gateway` value for `models.reasoning_effort` that omits the provider-specific reasoning block so a relay chooses the per-route protocol. The stated invariant is pinned by the new test: `gateway_reasoning_policy_omits_provider_specific_controls` drives the real adapter over HTTP against `FakeGateway` and asserts the recorded request body has no `reasoning` key while `usage.include` still reaches the wire, so a regression that forwarded `gateway` through the catch-all effort arm would fail it. The docs and the `.tinysweeper.toml` deployment change match the implementation, and the merge into `provider_options` keeps the provider pin and usage accounting intact for the new empty-object arm. The change looks sound to merge.

The change threads the actually-reviewed commit through `own_review_state` as a new `OwnReview { event, head_sha }` so a repeated approval is suppressed only for the exact commit already approved, while a changed or unknown head gets a fresh verdict. Every invariant the new comments claim is pinned by a test that fails without it: same-head suppression (`an_approval_that_already_stands_is_not_restated`), changed-head refresh (`a_clean_changed_head_receives_a_fresh_approval`, which fails under the old head-blind suppression), unknown-metadata refresh (`an_approval_without_a_known_reviewed_head_is_refreshed`), and the verdict's commit surviving later advisory comments (`own_review_metadata_keeps_the_verdict_commit_after_later_comments`, plus malformed-`commit_id` handling). The mock was updated in step — seeding captures the current head, pushes retain the reviewed commit, and comment-while-standing-verdict keeps the old entry — so the mock still mirrors GitHub's semantics the multi-push test relies on. The adapter parses `commit_id` defensively (null, non-string, empty all map to unknown, which errs toward re-approving rather than skipping). No defects found; safe to merge.

The change carries the reviewed commit alongside the standing verdict through the existing review-history read and suppresses a repeated approval only when the previous approval's commit matches the current head, exactly as the description states; changed, unknown, and same-head paths are each covered by in-crate tests, and the GitHub, mock, and port definitions stay consistent with no extra API request. The diff matches the description and looks sound to merge.
